core_obligations: Rank bookkeeping along the factorization (proof lines 3719-3755): each step of type (1) (gluing points on different components) leaves Pic(X)[l] unchanged and raises h^0 by 1; each step of type (2) (gluing on one component) fits 0 -> k^* -> Pic(X_i) -> Pic(X_{i+1}) -> 0 and lowers h^1 by 1; each step of type (3) (squishing a tangent vector) fits 0 -> (k,+) -> Pic(X_i) -> Pic(X_{i+1}) -> 0 and lowers h^1 by 1; since k is algebraically closed of characteristic prime to l, k^* and (k,+) are l-divisible with k^*[l] = F_l and (k,+)[l] = 0, so only steps of type (2) decrease the l-rank, by exactly 1.

Endpoint and count (proof lines 3757-3770): on the normalization h^1_n = g_geom and dim Pic(X_n)[l] = 2 g_geom; since g = h^1_0, the number of steps of type (2) and (3) is at most g - g_geom, whence dim Pic(X)[l] <= g - g_geom + 2 g_geom = g + g_geom.

Equality characterization (proof lines 3771-3783): equality holds iff no step of type (3) occurs, which by Lemma lemma-multicross means all singularities are multicross; conversely lemma-multicross supplies a sequence without type (3) steps (gluing the local sequences at the singular points; the author marks the gluing as details omitted).
proof_roadmap: Factor the normalization into point-gluing and tangent-squishing steps.
Track Pic[l]-rank and h^0, h^1 through the three step types using the l-divisibility of k^* and (k,+).
Read the endpoint values off the smooth projective normalization and count the available steps.
Characterize equality by the absence of squishing steps via lemma-multicross, in both directions.
difficulty_reason: The proposition bounds the l-torsion of Picard by g + g_geom and characterizes equality (statement lines 3700-3713). The proof (lines 3715-3783) runs a genuine rank bookkeeping over a factorization of the normalization into elementary modifications: three exact sequences on Picard with the l-divisibility of k^* and (k,+) deciding which steps change the rank, the endpoint values on the normalization, the counting bound g - g_geom, and the equality characterization through lemma-multicross in both directions. H3: the orchestration of the three step types with the divisibility analysis is a real argument, not a reference chase.
